question.problem: Consider the positively (outward) oriented surface $S$ given by $(x-3)^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=36$ and the vector field $F=(x+1)\,i-y\,j+z\,k.$ Use the divergence theorem to find the flux of $F$ across $S.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x+1)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(-y)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(z) \\  & =1+(-1)+1 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid sphere of radius $6$ enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}1\,\text{d}V \\  & =1{∭}_{R}\,\text{d}V \\  & =1\cdot \text{Volume}(R) \\  & =1\cdot \frac{4}{3}\pi \cdot {6}^{3} \\  & =288\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
